study_tips: Break your study time into short focused sessions, review regularly, and test yourself with small quizzes.
Use active recall and spaced repetition, and try to explain topics in your own words.
time_management: Start by listing your tasks, estimate how long each will take, and create a simple daily timetable you can follow.
Prioritize important subjects first, study in focused blocks, and schedule short breaks to avoid burnout.
exam_preparation: Review key concepts, solve past papers under timed conditions, and note the mistakes you make so you don't repeat them.
A day before the exam, focus on revising summaries and staying calm instead of learning everything from scratch.
subject_help_math: Revisit the basics with simpler problems, then gradually move to harder ones. Practice a few questions every day.
Watch step-by-step explanations, try to solve examples on your own, and check solutions only after you attempt them.
subject_help_science: For biology, create flashcards for key terms. For physics, practice problems and try to relate concepts to real life.
Draw diagrams and mind maps to connect ideas, and teach the topic to an imaginary student to test yourself.
exam_anxiety: Try deep breathing, short walks, and preparing a realistic study plan so you feel more in control.
Focus on progress, not perfection. Good preparation plus rest usually reduces exam stress a lot.
motivation: Set small daily goals, reward yourself when you complete them, and remind yourself why your studies matter to you.
Start with easy tasks to build momentum, and study with a friend or group if that keeps you accountable.
